building.name: Irving M. Scott School
building.completed_conflict: The assessor's roll gives 1900; the 2001 Dogpatch survey dates the Tennessee Street addition to 1895 and the school it replaced to 1877.

historical_record.description: The Outside Lands Committee set this parcel aside for a school, one of several it reserved in outlying sections of the city.
The San Francisco School Department built an eight-room frame school facing Minnesota Street, replacing the Potrero School of 1865 at Napa and Kentucky Streets.
An addition facing Tennessee Street. The school was renamed for the superintendent of Union Iron Works, who gave money towards its construction and equipment.
Schoolchildren from the school escorted President McKinley to the laying of the keel of the USS Ohio at Union Iron Works.

historic_survey.note: One of four public and civic buildings still standing in Dogpatch in 2001. Serving a working-class neighborhood, the school taught practical trades — cooking and homemaking for the girls, manual training for the boys.
